language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Welcome to the ball park. I'm Tony. Baseball is all about hitting homeruns and running very fast.
But in baseball we count everything. We count how many homeruns somebody hits or how hard he throws the ball.
This is all done very precisely. Whole numbers are not precise enough for us.
so we use small parts of a numbers to be more accurate.
Fractions and decimals help us in counting everything very precisely.
A fraction is a number that names a part of a whole or a part of a group.
It is written as two numbers separated by a bar.
The top number is called the numerator and the bottom number is called the denominator.
The numerator tells you the selected number of equal parts.
while the denominator tells you the total number of equal parts.
An example of a fraction is 1/2. In this example, there are two equal parts. You have only one of them.
Therefore, the number of parts you have as compared to the total is 1/2.
Fractions can also be mixed, meaning there is a whole number plus part of a number.
For instance, let’s say you have one and a half pizzas. The number would be written as 1-1/2.
As a decimal, a 1/2 would be written 0.5 In the pizza example, you would have 1.5 pizzas.
Remember, the numerator is how many pieces you have.
while the denominator is the total number of pieces.
